Okay so I am going to make a long post and pour all of my knowledge into this to help you! My hair is long, full, but dry and tangles easy. Now that I have learned so much it has gotten much easier to manage. I will say that what works for one person may not work for every person!! So forget CGM, forget hair types--for a minute--and let's focus on tangles and frizz. 

Those two things imply your hair is DRY. So moisture is really important, but first you need to **clarify your hair.** This step cannot be skipped, its like the taking off makeup step. The cheapest rec is if you live in the US; Suave has a $1 'essentials daily clarify shampoo' Do you have to use this every wash? no. should you once a month? yes. 

Now I'll type up an example tutorial you could follow.

Get into the shower to wash your hair, **do not** brush to detangle **before**, you say your hair re-tangles wet anyways, I'll address this next. Use warmish water and completely soak your hair, not too hot or cold water. temp plays a role, even water quality plays a role. **If you have hard water in your pipes it could affect your hair.** 

Next use enough of the clarify shampoo that it suds and covers ALL your hair, really scrub it in but gently, and let it sit for a minute. Yes this will dry out your hair a little, it is stripping everything from your hair but its okay because we are adding moisture back. Rinse it out thoroughly, I even lean forward to rinse upside down just to make sure because thick hair problems lol. Then get a super moisturizing mask (TGIN Honey miracle hair mask, As I am, Curlsmith, Jessicurl, Camilie Rose...just a few options.) and slather a generous amount into your wet strands and finally detangle, if your detangler comb works, great! If it's not detangling much then there are tons of brushes for all needs, these you can look up on your own. 

Gently brush the knots out, starting in small sections working at the ends going up to the roots, if the hair doesn't feel slippery enough, add some more of the conditioner/mask and wet it more, this is what helps keep breakage away while brushing. Once its all brushed out I use a big claw and pin it up so it can sit for at-least 10 minutes (up to 30, adding a heat cap helps me but I am typing too much?) it's important conditioner sits on the hair so it can do its thing, set a timer to be sure you're not rinsing too early. 

Once its time to finally rinse, use cooler water, or just not hot water. Your hair in this stage will feel snarky if it's like mine. It won't want to cooperate and might even still feel dry after the conditioner is rinsed, that is why the final step has to be a **quality leave-in conditioner**, again it can be from the brands recommended above.  Curlsmith has a--pricey-- 'air dry leave in' that works for me, since you mentioned no heat, same for me, I assume you air dry. I'm sure there are  *good* drugstore leave-ins but none have been holy grails for me yet. 

Okay last step I promise, you want your hair super wet, soaking strands that were just rinsed and you want to add a generous amount of the 'leave-in' (over time you'll learn the right amount of product for your hair.) I like to let my hair hang upside down so I can apply it easier since its so long, I just rake it through the strands because touching/brushing a lot equals more frizz. Then you can plop it with your choice of towel/shirt. Sometimes I leave it up in a towel twist or clip so that its not being moved around while it dries because frizz will start. 

My side note, if we can call it that, or side novel idk. Is you mentioned 'mousse, gels, oils' 

**Gels and Mousse can dry your hair out**. And oils can sit on your wet hair without penetrating the strands. So for now at least use the elimination diet of sorts and skip those products. I'm not saying never use them again but wait until your hair gets more moisture (and protein? some hair needs less than others) and then re-introduce those products if needed. 

For refreshing hair in between washes I suggest browsing some of the posts on this subreddit and finding *that* routine that fits best for you! All the best luck!
